content: Dosage Instructions for Intestinal Amebiasis Treatment: For patients aged 1-3 years: Administer 5 mL (equivalent to 100 mg) orally every 12 hours for 3 days. For patients aged 4-11 years: Administer 10 mL (equivalent to 200 mg) orally every 12 hours for 3 days. For patients aged 12 years and older: Administer 500 mg orally every 12 hours for 3 days. Safety and efficacy have not been established for children under 1 year of age. Drug Interactions: 1. Nitazoxanide and Axi-cabtagene Ciloleucel: Both drugs may enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 2. Nitazoxanide and Baricitinib: Nitazoxanide may increase baricitinib levels by reducing its elimination. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong OAT3 inhibitors is not recommended. 3. Side Effects: Common side effects include headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting, and chromaturia (discoloration of urine). Less common side effects include increased ALT levels, anorexia, increased appetite, elevated creatinine levels, sweating, dizziness, pale yellow eye discoloration, fever, flatulence, malaise, pruritus, and rash. Rare but serious allergic reactions may occur. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to nitazoxanide or any of its components. The liquid form contains sugar; use caution if you have diabetes. Safety in pregnant or breastfeeding women is not well established. Use only if clearly needed. Safety and efficacy in children under 1 year (for suspension) or under 12 years (for tablets) have not been established. Administration Instructions: Shake the liquid suspension well before each dose. Measure doses carefully using a proper measuring device. Take the medication with food. Complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Overdose: In case of overdose with severe symptoms (e.g., difficulty breathing), call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center.
